evidence.requirements: Every requirement in the brief is met. The start page lists title, date, time, price and "N seats left" (TastingCard.tsx:20-37, start.jpg). Each card has a "Book <title>" link (TastingCard.tsx:51-56). The form has fields labelled Name, Email and Guests (1 to 8) and a "Book" button (BookingPage.tsx:90-138). The server never allows more seats than are left, and the error appears on the field it concerns (booking-schema.ts:31-44, app.ts:74-83, form.jpg). The confirmation shows the heading "Booking confirmed", the tasting, guests, total price and reference (ConfirmationPage.tsx, confirmation.jpg). /staff has a Password field and a Sign in button, checked against STAFF_PASSWORD (index.ts:13, StaffPage.tsx:70-91). Staff see bookings grouped by tasting with name, email, guests and reference, and Cancel frees the seats (bookings.ts:62-76, staff.jpg). Fully booked state: TastingCard.tsx:46-49 and BookingPage.tsx:34-40. Phone layout is checked for horizontal overflow at 360 px (winery.spec.ts:144-154). React, Express, React Router, react-hook-form, zod and Tailwind are used. PORT defaults to 3000, bookings are in memory and start empty, the interface is in English. No unmet items.
evidence.correctness: The seat check and the reservation run in one synchronous path with no awaits (app.ts:74-83, bookings.ts:44-54), so concurrent requests cannot oversell. reserve() re-checks as a guard. seatsLeft is derived from the stored bookings, so cancelling (Map delete) frees seats right away. Boundaries are handled: guests must be a whole number from 1 to 8, NaN, strings and fractions are rejected, exactly the seats left is allowed, and a full tasting gets its own message (booking-schema.ts:31-44, booking-schema.test.ts). A body that is not an object returns 400 (app.ts:77-80), and malformed JSON maps to 400 (app.ts:151-155). If seats change while the form is open, the server rejects the booking and the error is mapped onto the field (BookingPage.tsx:76-80). References are unique (bookings.ts:100-109). Dates are formatted in UTC to avoid time-zone shifts (format.ts:14-23). No logic errors found.
evidence.security: The password check hashes both values with sha256 and compares them with timingSafeEqual (app.ts:201-205). The cookie holds only an opaque random id that maps to a server-side session with a 12-hour limit, so sign-out really revokes it (app.ts:111-114, 167-175). The cookie is httpOnly and SameSite=Lax, with a random signing key per start (app.ts:42-51). Sign-in is rate-limited (app.ts:92-100). The app uses helmet and a 10 kb JSON body limit (app.ts:40-41). Staff routes are guarded by requireStaff. The public confirmation leaves out name and email (bookings.ts:84-98). React escapes all output and there is no dangerouslySetInnerHTML. No secrets are in the code, and the app fails closed if STAFF_PASSWORD is unset (app.ts:101-103). Minor gaps: the cookie has no `secure` flag, and there is no trust-proxy setting for the rate limiter behind a reverse proxy.
evidence.code_quality: The code is clearly layered: shared zod schema and types, a small BookingBook domain class, an Express app factory with injectable options for tests, and React pages and components. Names are good, comments are short and say why, and errors are handled consistently ({message} or {errors}; ErrorPage and NotFoundPage on the client). The size fits the task. Small blemishes: long Tailwind class strings are repeated for buttons and alerts (BookingPage.tsx:135, StaffPage.tsx:88, 80, 151), and the mobile table cells repeat a lot of utility classes (StaffPage.tsx:198-221).
evidence.tests: There are four layers of tests. Schema unit tests cover boundaries, trimming, whole numbers, seats left and full tastings (booking-schema.test.ts). Supertest API tests cover listing, booking totals, unique references, invalid input per field, overbooking, booking exactly the seats left, a fully booked tasting, staff auth, wrong password, 503 when unconfigured, rate limiting, the 12-hour expiry, revocation of a copied cookie, the grouped staff view, and cancel freeing seats and allowing a re-book (api.test.ts). Testing Library tests cover the form's accessible error descriptions, the client-side seat check, a server-side rejection mapped to the field, and the confirmation (booking-flow.test.tsx). Playwright covers the full guest and staff journey plus a phone-overflow check (winery.spec.ts). The only thing not tested directly is truly concurrent requests, which the design relies on synchronous execution to prevent.
evidence.ux_design: The design is polished and fits a small winery: wine and cream palette, Cormorant serif headings, a gold accent rule, and well-spaced cards (start.jpg). The booking form shows a live total, a hint with seats left, and a clear red error under the email field (form.jpg). The confirmation is clean, with a prominent reference (confirmation.jpg). The staff page is tidy, grouped by tasting with booked/left counts (staff.jpg). There are states for few seats left and fully booked, and on mobile the table turns into stacked cards. Weaknesses: Cancel deletes a booking immediately with no confirmation and no success message (StaffPage.tsx:102-114), which is risky for staff. The footer still shows "Staff sign-in" while staff are signed in (Layout.tsx:40, staff.jpg).
evidence.accessibility: Inputs have real <label htmlFor> elements, and errors and hints are linked with aria-describedby and aria-invalid (TextField.tsx:20-36). There is a skip link and a main landmark (Layout.tsx:7-33), a visible focus-visible outline (styles.css:39-42), and regions labelled by tasting headings. Tables have a caption, th scope and an sr-only Actions header, and form-level errors use role=alert. html lang=en is set. Contrast looks sufficient (muted #6b5c55 and danger #9b2226 on near-white). Gaps: field-level errors have no live region and rely on react-hook-form moving focus to the first invalid field. On phones the staff table is set to display:block (StaffPage.tsx:182-197), which can strip table semantics for screen readers.
evidence.simplicity: The dependencies are all established and justified: express, cookie-session, helmet, express-rate-limit, react-router, react-hook-form, zod and tailwind. One zod schema is shared by client and server. The amount of code is modest (about 10 small client files, 4 server files), with no needless abstraction. The server-side session map on top of cookie-session adds a little, but it is documented and justified in SPEC.md:35.
evidence.maintainability: The README covers run, develop and test commands, environment variables, the layout, and the manual Playwright browser install (README.md). docs/SPEC.md documents decisions with reasons, the API contract, booking rules, pages and acceptance criteria. There is a full regression suite, package-lock.json pins dependencies, there are typecheck scripts, and engines requires node >=22. Missing: no CI pipeline configuration, no release or versioning approach (no changelog; version is fixed at 1.0.0), and no .nvmrc or exact Node pin. Staff usage is simple and implied by the README, but there is no separate staff note.

strengths: Correct, race-free seat logic with one shared zod schema validating on both client and server, so error messages are identical and shown on the right field
Strong security for the scope: timing-safe password check, revocable server-side sessions with a 12-hour limit, rate-limited sign-in, helmet, and a public confirmation without personal data
Thorough, meaningful tests at four levels (schema, API, component, end-to-end) that map directly to the brief, plus a polished, coherent winery design that works on phones
issues: No CI pipeline and no release or versioning approach in the repository, so the good test suite is not enforced automatically
Staff Cancel deletes a booking immediately with no confirmation, undo or success message (StaffPage.tsx:102-114), which is risky for winery staff

Smaller accessibility and hardening gaps: field errors are not in a live region, the mobile staff table uses display:block, and the session cookie has no secure flag or trust-proxy setting for deployment behind HTTPS
review.verdict: The app meets every requirement in the brief with correct, well-tested and securely handled booking and staff flows, wrapped in a polished design that suits the winery. It could ship to the winery almost as is; the fixes still worth making are a confirmation step for Cancel and a CI pipeline.
